properties.membership_rationale: A review with a proposed retinal hypercircuit framework, not an original implemented healthcare world model. Adapted demonstrations and the authors' earlier decoder remain attributed prior work.

properties.purpose: Research background for computational retinal neuroprosthesis design.
properties.contribution: Literature synthesis of visual encoding, neural computation and stimulus reconstruction.
properties.profile_rationale: BP_COMPONENT denotes background relevance to architectural responsibilities, not an implemented component or complete simulator.

properties.purpose: Proposed future computational improvement of electrode-based retinal prostheses.
properties.population_scope: Broad discussion of photoreceptor degeneration with preserved ganglion cells; no enrolled population or disease-specific eligibility protocol.
properties.decision_boundary: Decoded stimulus fidelity could help assess or adjust electrical stimulation patterns.
properties.authority: No implemented stimulation authority, human approval boundary or autonomy level established.

properties.proposal: Combine feature-based and sampling-based visual computation using feedforward, recurrent and winner-take-all motifs.
properties.functional_flow_discussed: Presented visual stimulus → neural-response encoding → spike patterns → spike-to-image conversion → reconstructed stimulus. Reconstruction fidelity is proposed as a possible stimulation-assessment signal.
alternatives_discussed: CNN encoders and image reconstruction networks
Probabilistic graphical models and spiking neural-network inference
properties.implementation_boundary: No original integrated implementation or evaluation of the proposed hypercircuit is established. Hybrid network motifs do not automatically mean operational mechanistic–learned world dynamics.

prior_examples.Figure 3: Adapted retinal encoding examples: one ganglion cell, five bipolar-cell subunits; CNN with two convolutional layers and one dense layer.
prior_examples.Figure 4: Previously developed spike-image decoder: dense converter and image-image autoencoder. The illustrated preparation is salamander retina. The width 512 is not patient count or propagated-state size.
prior_examples.Figure 5: Adapted photoreceptor, MRF/WTA and denoising examples.

non_entailments: Encoding and reconstruction do not establish a successor-state transition.
Neural sampling and inference dynamics do not establish future-trajectory uncertainty or calibration.
Recurrent motifs and HMM diagrams do not establish an implemented world model.
The paper's encoding/decoding use of closed-loop terminology does not demonstrate therapeutic control.

assertions.rationale: The animal example and data link identify provenance context, but do not establish variable-level source, units, timestamps, transformations and version retention in the proposed framework.
Spike timing is important in the review, but retention or reversible recovery of native observation times at a declared processing resolution is not documented for the proposal.
Acquisition time is not distinguished from processed-signal availability, and no training or query procedure enforcing information-release times is reported.
No measured/missing/invalid indicator is specified. An interval with no spikes must not be interpreted as missing recording or valid silence without an explicit validity convention.
No per-variable freshness representation or carry-forward update rule is provided. The unresolved acquisition design does not establish either use or inapplicability.
Discussion of spike timing and neural dynamics does not supply a proposal-specific prediction rule using actual unequal observation intervals.
Retinal stimulus-response encoding is discussed, but no framework-specific model represents when, whether or why observations become available conditional on acquisition context.
No target/grid-specific witness-preservation test is reported. Biological timing importance does not establish an observation-clock audit or permit a clock-regime assignment.
No target measurement schema or traceable unit/terminology conversions are specified. Correspondences between biological circuits and neural-network motifs are not data harmonization.
No original split, stimulus/recording overlap audit, preprocessing-fit boundary or availability audit is supplied. A public data link establishes neither leakage control nor leakage.
No site-local data retention, exchanged artifacts or federated training/query protocol is described.
Encoding is explicitly reviewed and recommended. Adapted CNN examples do not establish an operational encoder belonging to the future integrated framework, as required by this implementation feature.
No named pretrained checkpoint and adaptation procedure is specified. Transferring computational ideas from cortex to retina is not checkpoint reuse.
No implemented context-to-target-representation loss is specified for the proposal. Biological spikes, hidden variables and an autoencoder bottleneck alone do not meet this criterion.
No qualifying predictive-representation objective or anti-collapse mechanism is supplied. WTA competition and biological inhibition are not demonstrated anti-collapse controls for such an objective.
Reconstruction is central to the review and prior decoder. Its executed loss is not established for the new integrated proposal; details and earlier results remain attributed to [76], not inherited.
Combining computational approaches is not a specified fusion operation over two input modalities. Serial stimulus-to-spike-to-image mappings do not establish multimodal fusion.
No fusion rule conditioned on modality availability, quality or recency, or defined missing-modality behavior, is reported.
Recurrent motifs and HMMs are reviewed, but no implemented carried state/history is defined for the integrated proposal. This does not deny states in the cited methods.
The probabilistic-coding discussion supplies no proposal-specific posterior/filter over hidden state conditioned on observation history.
Encoding and decoding are not separate prior propagation and observation correction operations. No missing-observation correction semantics are specified.
An adjustable device is envisaged, but updating a maintained individual state from arriving measurements during sequential use is not reported.
The precision-medicine motivation is not a patient-specific parameter or weight-adaptation rule. Fitting receptive fields in cited work is not adaptation by the proposal.
Multiple applications and computational examples are discussed, but the same maintained state/checkpoint feeding at least two typed tasks is not established.
No original ablation tests omitted state/history against specified targets. Adapted receptive-field comparisons are not sufficiency tests of the integrated proposal.
Spike-history filters and recurrent networks belong to reviewed approaches; an operational history-conditioning mechanism is not assigned to the integrated proposal.
No matched history-swap, withholding or population-prior control tests individual predictive value. Personalized-device aspirations and animal decoding do not establish it.
No transition-level identity/anatomy memory, constraint or consistency loss is specified. Qualitative reconstruction similarity is insufficient.
Biological explanations and adapted filter visualizations do not define an inspectable maintained state of the proposal. Gap-junction function remains an explicit uncertainty.
Recurrent motifs motivate future work, but no executed memory/read mechanism or context window is specified for the integrated framework.
Stimulation is an envisaged operation, but no settable command is shown to condition a relevant prediction. Presented visual inputs are not automatically therapeutic-action queries.
The narrative distinguishes visual input, neural responses and stimulation, but supplies no operational action vocabulary with role/effect-channel typing.
Electrode targeting, stimulation parameters, units, timing and duration sufficient for an interpretable or executable query are not specified.
No stimulation start/stop times, command cadence or duration semantics are given. Spike-recording time is not an intervention schedule.
No joint stimulation-command or replacement/partial-update/inheritance semantics are defined. Multiple electrodes alone would not establish coherent bundle handling.
Operational stimulation bounds, contraindications and candidate restrictions are unreported. Reconstruction fidelity is not a hard action constraint.
Retinal stimulation is recognizable conceptually, but no calibrated mapping from an operational action representation or desired spike pattern to executable commands is established.
No context-conditioned coverage, overlap or mechanistic-support criterion is estimated and tested for candidate stimulation alternatives.
No reported experiment compares predicted successors under two specified stimulation alternatives from the same initial context. Comparing reconstruction methods is not L3 action comparison.
Physical reversibility, residual effects and harm after stopping stimulation are not assessed for the proposal.

capability_assessments.rationale: This classifies the fully inspected contribution as review/background, not every cited method. Explicit review wording, prior-work figure attribution and future-work wording support the classification. The linked feature assertions record unestablished implementation/evaluation, not proven mechanism absence. No original healthcare state-transition artifact or WM-inspired representation evaluation is established; L0–L4 are not inherited from references. Decoding the presented stimulus is not successor-state prediction.

scope.population: No enrolled population; explicit future integrated retinal-prosthesis framework.

gate_assessments.rationale: BP_COMPONENT is selected for a conceptual literature-review contribution, not an original empirical predictive system with development/test data. The prior animal-data illustration does not create such a system. Any implementation or data reuse requires its own data/leakage assessment.

The review does not claim its own implemented temporal world model. Applying a transition acceptance test to the review as an empirical model would misidentify the contribution. Proposal-specific transition evidence remains not_reported rather than absent.

For the envisaged function affecting retinal stimulation, operational guards, abstention, fallback, stimulation limits and hazard-validation evidence are not reported. No pass or observed safety failure is inferred.

This artifact is a review/proposal, not a versioned operational release. Data links and cited implants do not constitute release of the proposed framework. Future device governance requires a separate product/use/jurisdiction assessment.
